claims.claim: Guardrails are runtime checks that run during generation and can modify or block LLM responses, using the same check types as assertions/evals
Diagram: Guardrails = runtime enforcement, can abort streaming, policy compliance, defined in PromptConfig
Diagram: Assertions = test verification, checked after complete, defined in Scenario

Table: guardrails enforce policies during generation, can abort early while streaming, defined in PromptConfig, failure = policy violation; assertions run after generation, defined in Scenario, failure = test failure
On a guardrail failure the assistant message is rewritten in place; the pipeline continues and no error is returned
A streaming guardrail that triggers replaces or truncates the chunk and stops reading the stream; the turn completes with no error
Guardrails are defined in the 'validators' section under spec of a PromptConfig
Validator YAML shape: type, params, message, fail_on_violation are valid keys
'message' sets the user-facing text shown when a guardrail fires; default policy message if omitted
During pack compilation packc folds 'message' into params['message']
The validators table lists type, params, message, enabled and id; the page documents no fail_on_violation field
Content blockers (banned_words / content_excludes) replace content with the message or a default policy message
Length guards (max_length / length) truncate content to the configured maximum
Any other check type that triggers replaces the content with message, the check's own replacement, or the default blocked message
With fail_on_violation false the guardrail evaluates, records results in message.Validations, and does not modify content (monitor-only)
Any check type can be used as a guardrail
Alias pairs: content_excludes/banned_words, max_length/length, sentence_count/max_sentences, field_presence/required_fields
content_excludes and max_length support streaming
sentence_count and field_presence do not support streaming
Guardrails that are not streaming-capable run on the completed response and replace the content when they trigger
field_presence / required_fields is not streaming-capable and replaces the content when any field is missing
Streaming-capable guardrails abort generation immediately when a violation is detected
Diagram: chunk 3 containing a banned word aborts the stream
The stage stops using the stream but reads the remainder in the background, so the provider still generates the remaining tokens
Combined example: banned_words params.words (list), max_length params max_characters and max_tokens, each with a message
The page documents no separate max_sentences guardrail example; the combined example uses banned_words and max_length
Streaming-capable guardrails run on each chunk; every guardrail then runs on the completed response in declaration order
First failure stops the validation chain
Content Safety example: banned_words with words list including '100%' and a message
Response Length example: max_length with max_characters 2000, max_tokens 500
Scenario assertion guardrail_triggered takes params guardrail: banned_words and assertions: true plus message
Declaration order does not change when streaming guardrails fire
Custom guardrails implement hooks.ProviderHook
Go snippet: sdk.Open("./app.pack.json", "chat", sdk.WithProviderHook(&MyCustomHook{}))
